P1: Any community that lasts is going to get reorganized by attraction and pair-bonding. In a city, two exes can move across town. In a thirty-person commune? They might still be sharing a kitchen the next morning, plus a work team, a meeting, childcare and friends. So a couple's jealousy or breakup becomes the community's problem, because it changes loyalties and sleeping arrangements. It changes who does what work, and things with the children, and alliances. Sometimes it changes who leaves.
P2: The usual argument is monogamy versus free love, and that starts one level too late. My Romance Guide has the longer version. Here I'll just say the community problem plainly: living in close quarters makes jealousy bigger, and jealousy can capture either system.
P3: Rigid monogamy can turn fear and possession into a moral law. Free love without inner pl/ork can spread the same fear across a bigger spreadsheet. And a relationship label doesn't release childhood panic. Or comparison, or abandonment terror, or the wish to control another person.
P4: I don't think a community should choose the form for everyone. Couples can make different agreements, and so can people in other relationship configurations. They can revise those agreements, too. And when the agreements bring up old material, they can ask for support.
P5: Whatever forms people choose, their housing shouldn't depend on staying inside one romantic agreement. Neither should their children's security, or their membership, or their access to common necessities.
P6: ZEGG and Tamera have been experimenting with relationships inside community for decades. Their answers aren't commandments for everybody. What they do show is that a group can acknowledge erotic life. It doesn't have to pretend twenty adults have become neutral colleagues because the bylaws say so.
P7: For me, the non-negotiable is that jealousy can't become the hidden governor. People have to be able to speak about it, and feel it in the body. They have to be able to explore it without being humiliated. And it has to be released gradually, not turned into punishment or policy.
P8: The group can offer support and enforce basic boundaries without choosing everyone's relationship structure. People will still disagree, and that's more realistic than declaring the matter solved.
